q1_issues.issue: "sunlight, carbon dioxide and water" is encoded as three Patient atoms on ONE turn event, whereas coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default (one event per conjunct) and the collective single-event form is licensed only for reciprocal/aggregate predicates and is described only for multiple Agent atoms.
The fused compound kind carbon_dioxide is emitted without its mandatory genus atom (Inheritance carbon_dioxide dioxide), which the Compound-kind rule says is always emitted.

q2_gaps: transformation resultative "turn X into Y" — the Resultatives section covers only a STATE result (reified state + flat atom + Result) and a MOTION result (Source/Goal); a change-of-substance result has no described form, so "into sugars" was given the motion-result head Goal

a jointly-combining (aggregate) reading of coordinated OBJECTS — the collective escape hatch is worded for multiple Agent atoms on reciprocal/aggregate verbs, and there is no form for several objects consumed together by one event

a bare relational generic ("Trees use photosynthesis": bare kind NP on both sides, the stated trigger for the opaque kind-relation form) that also carries a purpose infinitive — the kind-relation form reifies no event for the purpose head (To) to attach to, so the two rules conflict
notes: The bare-plural generic rule shape, the Skolem-function events, Theme on "use", the purpose head (To <main> <purpose>) with the main action first, and the 0.9/0.9 empirical generic TV are all correct. The mass constants sunlight/water/sugar and the absent tense atom are also right.
